name: Dusty marigold
lede: Dusty marigold is a muted golden orange, ColorHub's English name for the Japanese traditional color Kikuchiba, "golden fallen leaves."

sections.title: Golden fallen leaves, and a shade of turmeric
sections.body:
Kikuchiba (黄朽葉) appears in the Wikipedia list of Japan's traditional colors as "golden fallen leaves" [1]. The same source also lists Ukon-iro, "turmeric-colored," as a related name for a near-identical shade, about 1.4 ΔE2000 units from this one in our library, close enough to read as the same color on screen [1][3].

The nearest named colors on file are [[saratoga]] and [[indian-yellow]], at 3 and 3.7 ΔE [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 311 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.3 percent, as photographed [2]. The earliest match is a 1250 diptych of the Crucifixion and the Madonna and Child by Bonaventura Berlinghieri, where it covers about a fifth of the panel, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. The rate is highest in a sample of 731 paintings from the 1820s, more than four times the archive's overall rate for that decade [2]. George Dawe's fifty sampled paintings contain it ten times, the highest rate among the painters checked, ahead of Lucas Cranach the Elder and Pierre Bonnard [2]. It is also more common than average in paintings from India, the United Kingdom, Sweden, Italy and Germany [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
